subject: Concealing cables and equipment
hook: Hidden cables are planned before the unit is built, not tidied up after it is fitted.
ig:
Hidden cables are planned before the unit is built, not tidied up after it is fitted.

If you are planning a media wall or TV unit this winter, settle these five things first:

1. List every device. Soundbar, router, console, set-top box: each needs power, a route and a shelf it fits on.
2. Put sockets where the kit lives. Your electrician can place them behind the TV and inside the equipment area before anything is fitted.
3. Plan the cable route. A void behind the back panel and cable holes in the right places carry everything out of sight.
4. Let it breathe. Closed cupboards need ventilation gaps or slatted fronts, because equipment gets warm.
5. Think about signal. Solid doors can block remotes and weaken Wi-Fi.

Get these right at the design stage and there is nothing to hide later.

Save this for when you start planning, and find our media walls through the link in bio.
fb:
With darker evenings and more time on the sofa, the tangle of cables under the TV starts to get noticed.

The secret to a media wall with no visible cables is simple: it is planned before anything is built. List your devices, get sockets placed where the equipment will sit, design a route behind the unit, and think about airflow and remote signals for anything hidden behind doors.
